messages:
anya: Quick sync — we need to settle on the SDK surface for retries + pagination. RFC suggested a RetryPolicy object but some folks want simple kwargs/flags for ergonomics. Which direction for Python/TS/Go?

infra-bot: RFC link: https://redwood.internal/rfcs/retry-pagination-surface (summary pinned) :link: 

mike: vote for a single canonical model but expose language-idiomatic shims. i.e. canonical RetryPolicy shape + small wrappers in each SDK. Python can use a dataclass, TS an interface, Go opts.

claire: agree. also: we need a stable header for idempotency if transports want to do server-side dedupe. propose header X-Redwood-Idempotency-Key.

jay: pagination edge-case: when iterating pages, retries mid-iteration can be tricky. if a page request is retried we must ensure resume token semantics don't double-skip or repeat items. prefer client-side resume that re-requests from token, not server replay.

mike: concrete ergonomics sketches — keep these short: 
Python: 
```
from redwood import Client, RetryPolicy
client.list_items(retry=RetryPolicy(max_attempts=4, backoff="expo", jitter=True))
```
TS: 
```
client.listItems({ retry: { maxAttempts: 4, backoff: 'expo' } })
```
Go (option pattern): 
```go
client.ListItems(ctx, req, client.WithRetry(client.RetryPolicy{MaxAttempts:4}))
```

anya: Those look good. question: do we accept both bool/flags and full objects? users like one-liners (retry=True) but advanced users need objects.

claire: we can support a union: bool | RetryPolicy in Python/TS via overloads. In Go provide WithRetrySimple(true) helper + WithRetryPolicy for full control. Keep defaults sensible (3 attempts, 200ms base, expo).

jay: pagination + retries: propose these rules: 
- For paged list endpoints, page fetches are retryable only if request is read-only and server returns an opaque page_token.
- Client should attach an idempotency token for multi-page iterators so if we have to restart the iterator we can continue without duplication server-side.
- Avoid retrying mutating operations unless user explicitly opts in.

mike: implementation detail: do we serialize RetryPolicy into transport metadata for observability? e.g. transport header X-Redwood-RetryMeta: {policy-json} — helps debug fallbacks. But we should be careful with size and PII.

claire: maybe only send a compact fingerprint (policy id + hash). full policy stays client-side/telemetry. that keeps requests small.

anya: decision proposal (vote): 
1) Canonical RetryPolicy object as source-of-truth.
2) Language shims: Python dataclass, TS interface + builder, Go option helpers.
3) High-level convenience param allowed (retry=True / retry=3 / retry={}) that maps into canonical policy.
4) Add X-Redwood-Idempotency-Key header for iterator operations; SDKs generate and attach when iterating pages automatically.
5) Transport may surface a compact Retry fingerprint header for debugging, not full JSON.

jay: +1 on rules. add test matrix for page-resume + failover.

mike: +1 but caution: automatic idempotency tokens could mask bugs for users who intentionally want per-request tokens. make it opt-out: sdk.iter_items(auto_idempotency=True) default True but user can pass idempotency_key manually or disable.

claire: we'll need docs and migration notes. also update API lint to require page_token opaque and stable.

devops-bot: NOTE: update required in transport impls: ensure header passthrough and add test coverage for GCP/AZURE LB behavior (sticky header).

anya: Action items: 
- Mike: draft the follow-up RFC that specifies canonical RetryPolicy JSON schema + fingerprinting approach.
- Claire: update SDK convention doc + TS/PY overload examples.
- Jay: add pagination-resume testcases and a small harness for injected failures.
- Infra: ensure transport header passthrough and document header name.

anya: I'll open the umbrella PR referencing RFC once Mike posts. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

mike: I'll aim to draft the RFC by EOD tomorrow.

claire: I'll start the TS + python PR templates today.

jay: putting tests on my board.

anya: resolving thread for now — we'll follow up with the RFC link here. :white_check_mark:
